I found six functions in the library source (`*/src`, test code excluded) that call `tokio::task::yield_now` directly:

- **`tokio/src/time/clock.rs`**: `advance` calls `crate::task::yield_now().await` after it moves the paused clock forward.
- **`tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/trace.rs`**: `TraceStatus.start_trace_request` and `TraceStatus.end_trace_request` each call `crate::task::yield_now().await` inside their compare-exchange loops.
- **`tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread_alt/trace.rs`**: has the same two `TraceStatus` methods. The file is identical to the one above apart from its `Handle` import.
- **`tokio-util/src/task/spawn_pinned.rs`**: `LocalWorkerHandle.run` calls `runtime.block_on(tokio::task::yield_now())` in its drain loop.

I left these out:
- Every hit in `tokio/src/mpsc`, `tokio/src/loom`, `tokio/src/runtime/time/tests` and the other `thread::yield_now` sites, because they are `std::thread::yield_now` or the loom wrapper.
- The scheduler `yield_now` methods in `worker.rs`, `task/mod.rs` and `harness.rs`.
- Doc-comment examples, in `builder.rs`, `join_map.rs`, `spawn.rs` and others.
- Test-only code that sits inside the library crates. That covers the `#[cfg(test)]` module in `signal/registry.rs` (`smoke`) and the files under `tokio/src/runtime/tests/` and `tokio/src/sync/tests/`. If you count those as library code, they would be extra entries.
